claim: AAAI 2026 accepted BayesAgent/vPGM, a framework where LLM agents follow probabilistic-graphical-model principles expressed in natural language ('verbalized'), then refines the resulting posteriors via actual numerical Bayesian inference -- validating verbalized/primed elicitation of structured probabilistic signal as an accepted mechanism.
stance_target: verbalized/primed elicitation of structured confidence signal (structurally analogous to DPRC's digit-priming readout) as an acceptable AAAI mechanism
scope_conditions: agentic reasoning under uncertainty, close-ended and open-ended tasks
quoted_support: Verbalized Probabilistic Graphical Modeling (vPGM), a Bayesian agentic framework that (i) guides LLM agents in following key principles of PGMs through natural language and (ii) refines the resulting posterior distributions via numerical Bayesian inference.

claim: vPGM avoids requiring expert-driven probabilistic model design, positioning itself as more broadly applicable than traditional PGM approaches -- a 'generality/no manual engineering' framing.
stance_target: generality as a framing dimension AAAI reviewers reward
quoted_support: Unlike many traditional probabilistic methods requiring substantial domain expertise, vPGM bypasses expert-driven model design, making it well-suited for scenarios with limited assumptions.

claim: The BayesAgent paper reports improvements on BOTH confidence calibration AND text generation quality as dual headline results, rather than calibration alone -- suggesting AAAI-accepted calibration-adjacent papers often pair calibration gains with a task-performance gain.
stance_target: pairing calibration metrics with task-performance metrics as an accepted framing
quoted_support: Our results indicate that the model effectively enhances confidence calibration and text generation quality.

claim: The paper underwent 4 arXiv revisions across roughly 19 months (June 2024 to January 2026) before/around AAAI 2026 acceptance, suggesting a long incubation and multiple review/revision cycles are common for accepted AAAI uncertainty papers.
stance_target: typical timeline from preprint to AAAI acceptance
